body:
How I selected these designers

This is an editorial selection of individual designers and personal practices, not an objective ranking and not a list of agencies.

For each entry I checked a live site for three things: a New York base, independent or freelance work, and a focus on identity or brand systems.

Two designers who appeared in the previous version of this guide have been removed in this update.

One had let her domain lapse and left no trace of a current practice; the other now states on her own site that she is looking for a full-time role.

A roundup is only useful if the people in it can still be hired, so I would rather publish a shorter list than a stale one.

Where a designer’s own site raises a question — limited availability, a concurrent in-house job, a portfolio that has not been updated — I say so in their entry.

Locations and services are self-reported, so confirm current availability, who will do the work, and project fit when you make contact.

Past agency projects should be read alongside the credits on each portfolio: working on a project is not the same as having designed it.

This guide is deliberately local, so for the history of the craft and the general hiring framework, see my companion guide to the best logo designers of all time.

24 independent brand identity designers in NYC

Use the specialties below to build a shortlist, then read complete projects rather than judging anyone from a single mark.

  1. Barbiana Liu
  2. Nicole Pivirotto
  3. Brooke Qualman
  4. Laci Harmon

1. Barbiana Liu

Barbiana Liu is a New York creative director and brand designer who works through her own practice, Leche Studio.

Based in New York City.

Focus Brand identity, websites and content design.

Her public portfolio includes Scattered Kind, Scenery Modern Supplements and Studio Petra, which together show how she carries one visual idea from logo into packaging and web.

Her work lives on Behance rather than a personal site, so ask for a full project walkthrough before you commit.

Consider for Lifestyle and wellness brands that want identity and digital design handled by one person.

2. Nicole Pivirotto

Nicole Pivirotto is an independent creative director, designer and author based in Brooklyn.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Visual identities, design systems and art direction.

Her identity work includes Gelée, Rank & Style and Busayo, and her wider portfolio includes Bala and Carolina Bucci.

Project inquiries go to a studio address, a small sign that she runs this as a practice rather than as occasional side work.

Consider for Consumer, wellness and lifestyle businesses that need a complete visual world, not only a mark.

3. Brooke Qualman

Brooke Qualman describes herself as a freelance brand designer and design director building strategic, cohesive brand systems.

Based in New York City.

Focus Brand design and creative direction for CPG, lifestyle and hospitality.

Her portfolio includes Fields Good Chicken, Hu Kitchen, Melt Shop and Fruit Fusion by Bath & Body Works.

Hers is the clearest freelance positioning on this list: the category she serves and the way she works are both stated up front.

Consider for Food, hospitality and consumer brands that need identity across packaging, menus, signage and web.

4. Laci Harmon

Laci Harmon is a Brooklyn brand designer and illustrator working with founders and growing businesses.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Identity, packaging and illustration.

Her portfolio includes Mothaplant, Maison Vorani, The High Prophet and work for D&AD.

Her site lists availability for freelance projects and for full-time roles, so confirm her capacity before you plan a timeline around her.

Consider for Founders who want a hand-drawn character running through identity and packaging together.

5. Tony Safran

Tony Safran runs the independent creative practice Butchy’s out of Brooklyn.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Brand identity, positioning, marketing and merchandise.

His portfolio includes New Balance Trail, Under Armour Run Club, Arbor Skateboards and the Los Angeles Times.

The work leans toward sport and apparel graphics, so judge it on how a mark behaves on product rather than on a letterhead.

Consider for Brands whose identity has to live on apparel, merchandise and campaign work.

6. Adam Ho

Adam Ho runs an independent studio practice from Queens, focused on large-scale identities for emerging technology companies.

Based in Queens.

Focus Brand identity, image-making and interaction design.

His portfolio includes Jasper, Paradigm, ENS, Coinbase and Nike ISPA.

He previously held in-house roles at Cash App and Zendesk, which shows in how his systems are built to survive inside a product team.

Consider for Technology companies that want an expressive identity built to work in a live product.

7. Gurjinder Singh

Gurjinder Singh positions himself as a freelance brand designer for B2B software that is hard to explain.

Based in New York, working remotely worldwide.

Focus Brand and web design for fintech and B2B.

His portfolio includes Social Alchemy, Therabrand and BeaconDx, and he works through his own entity, Gesso Studio.

His own résumé also lists a current senior brand designer role at Coinbound, so ask directly how much project capacity he has.

Consider for Companies with a complex product that needs a clearer story before it needs a new logo.

8. Daniel Koppich

Daniel Koppich lists his current status plainly as freelance and independent practice, based in Brooklyn.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Identity, exhibition and editorial design.

He was an associate partner at Pentagram from 2021 to 2023, after seven years at The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

His portfolio includes Wolff Olins, the Queens Museum, the Getty Museum and the Goethe-Institut.

This is institutional and cultural work rather than small-business identity, so match the brief before you reach out.

Consider for Cultural, architectural and institutional projects that need identity across several formats.

9. Arek Dvornechuck

Putting myself on my own list is awkward, so here is the case stated plainly and you can judge it.

Based in Brooklyn, New York City.

Focus Brand strategy, identity, web design and motion.

I have over 20 years of design experience, worked with Chermayeff & Geismar & Haviv and with agencies in Poland, and have been fully freelance since 2016.

Recent identity work includes Airport Executive, a London chauffeur service rebranded around an aviation-inspired monogram that runs from a chauffeur badge to airport signage.

Also Fox Berman, a Caribbean law firm with a custom inktrap wordmark, and SweetGrass, a Mississippi dispensary built on Art Deco lettering and bespoke packaging.

And Periti Digital, a HubSpot consultancy working across Dublin, Lisbon and Munich, where the verbal identity mattered as much as the mark.

I work at a flat $3,000 per week with no hourly billing, and a full brand identity is delivered in one week.

Consider for A direct relationship with a senior designer across strategy, identity, websites and motion.

10. Suze Myers

Suze Myers is a graphic designer and art director building brands, websites and books in Brooklyn.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Brand identity and websites for small businesses and solo creatives.

Her logo work includes Wuwu Nails, Ohayo House and Long Future Farms.

She sells defined branding packages covering a logo system, type, color and a brand book, which makes her scope easy to compare against a quote.

Consider for An owner-led business that wants a clear, fixed branding package rather than an open-ended engagement.

11. Eric W Lee

Eric W Lee is a Brooklyn freelance graphic designer specializing in logos, branding, packaging and illustration.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Logo systems, branding and illustration.

His portfolio includes NPR Music, KEXP, Crooked Media, the American Museum of Natural History and Hudson Yards.

His site carries a live availability link, which is the kind of signal worth checking before you build a shortlist.

Consider for Brands that want characterful illustration integrated into the logo and visual system.

12. Johanna Nager

Johanna Nager is a Queens-based web and brand identity designer.

Based in Queens.

Focus Web, identity and packaging.

Her portfolio includes Outdoor Voices, Jasper Health, Medik8 and Ultra Pouches.

Her site currently reads as open for work rather than describing a freelance practice, so clarify whether she is taking projects or looking for a role.

Consider for A project that connects a visual identity with packaging or a website.

13. Adrienne Hapanowicz

Adrienne Hapanowicz is a Brooklyn-based independent designer, art director and visual artist.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Design and art direction, with branding on selected projects.

Her portfolio includes Jazz Is Dead, National Geographic and an identity project for Adé.

The site is still labelled as a 2024 portfolio, so ask what she has shipped since and whether identity is a core service for her now.

Consider for Clients who want strong art direction and are comfortable briefing a generalist.

14. Mike Tully

Mike Tully is an independent designer in New York City working across identity, editorial and exhibitions.

Based in New York City.

Focus Cultural identity, editorial and exhibition design.

His projects include Perspecta 56 for the Yale architectural journal, Walden with Hugh Hayden at Lisson Gallery, and The Brooklyn Rail, where he was design director.

This is arts and editorial work first, so expect a reading-led process rather than a packaged brand offer.

Consider for Arts and cultural projects where identity has to work with editorial content or an exhibition.

15. Shruti Agrawal

Shruti Agrawal labels herself a freelance product and brand designer in Brooklyn.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Brand identity, strategy and digital product design.

Her portfolio includes Tripadvisor, the ACLU, Microsoft and Chase.

Product design leads her practice, so she is a better fit when the interface matters as much as the mark.

Consider for A brand identity that has to carry straight through into a usable digital product.

16. Graham Clifford

Graham Clifford runs an independent design and art direction practice from a studio on Little West 12th Street.

Based in New York City.

Focus Brand identity and art direction.

His portfolio includes SKYY vodka, Vineyard Vines and the Detroit Department of Transportation.

He came up through advertising, which shows in work built to be seen at distance rather than admired in a case study.

Consider for Clients who want an identity specialist with decades of brand and advertising experience.

17. Rebecca Matt

Rebecca Matt is an independent art director and brand designer in New York City.

Based in New York City.

Focus Identity systems and art direction.

Her portfolio includes the Hotel Chelsea, El Quijote and Villa Miami.

Her hospitality work is the clearest demonstration on this list of an identity designed for a physical place.

Consider for Hospitality and property brands that need identity designed with signage, print and interiors in mind.

18. Sam Bumbalo

Sam Bumbalo has been a full-time freelancer since 2021, working from Brooklyn on graphic systems and typography.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Identity systems, typography and illustration.

His portfolio includes the KinGin restaurant identity, the Google Fiber brand relaunch and Floyd.

He previously designed at Red Antler and Order, and interned at Pentagram on Paula Scher’s team and at Turner Duckworth.

Consider for Brands that want a typographic identity with room for illustration and motion.

19. Kevin Ebrahimoff

Kevin Ebrahimoff runs I’m Off Design, an independent freelance design studio in Brooklyn.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Brand identity, packaging and Shopify websites.

His client work includes She’s the Sauce, Cranky Cloud Coffee and Lavari Jewelers.

His site publishes the month he is next booking, which tells you more about real availability than most portfolios do.

Consider for A product business bringing brand, packaging and an online store together in one project.

20. Erica Bech

Erica Bech is a freelance creative director in Brooklyn who works on the organizing idea before the visuals.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Brand ideas, campaigns and creative direction.

Her page describes the approach rather than naming clients, so you will need to ask for work examples directly.

She also lists bookings opening in early 2027, which rules her out for anything urgent.

Consider for Brands that already have a designer and need a senior creative partner to set direction.

21. Maria Cynthia

Maria Cynthia is a brand and packaging designer whose site lists both Brooklyn and Jakarta.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Brand identity and packaging.

Her portfolio includes the Nectara identity and packaging, an American Folk Art Museum rebranding project and Gladly snack packaging.

Because she lists two cities, confirm which time zone she works in before you agree a review schedule.

Consider for Consumer brands weighing identity and packaging as a single decision.

22. Matthew Lewicki

Matthew Lewicki is a Brooklyn designer working across interface, visual identity and printed matter.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Visual identity, print and product design.

His portfolio includes All Things Go Music Festival, MedStar Health and Sam’s Listening Bar.

He also holds a current lead product designer role at Tone.audio, so treat his identity work as selective rather than full-time freelance.

Consider for Businesses whose identity has to connect print, culture and a digital interface.

23. Luciana Diehl

Luciana Diehl has run her own Brooklyn design business since 2017, pairing identity with Squarespace websites.

Based in Brooklyn, usually working remotely.

Focus Brand identity and Squarespace websites.

Her client work includes The Naptown Yogi, Get Lost in Italy and the New York Forró Festival.

She works directly with owners, which keeps the brand and the website in one conversation instead of two.

Consider for Small businesses that want a personal process and a site they can update themselves.

24. Ronin Wood

Ronin Wood is a Brooklyn graphic designer who takes select freelance work alongside a full-time life as a dad.

Based in Brooklyn.

Focus Campaign identity, print and graphic design.

His portfolio includes Brooklyn Brewery, 404 Media and Magic Spoon.

He is explicit that this is part-time and selective, which is useful honesty but makes him the wrong choice for a deadline-driven launch.

Consider for Organizations that need a clear visual voice across campaigns, print and community communications.

New York brand identity studios, if you need a team

If your project needs more hands than one person has, these are the New York studios I would explore.

Each one is a different shape of team rather than a different price point for the same service.

Gretel

Gretel is a Brooklyn studio on Clifton Place that sums up its work in three words: we create clarity.

Its projects include the Philadelphia Museum of Art, Finer Sounds and Hija de Sanchez.

Worth a look when strategy and design need to arrive as one answer.

Order

Order is a design office in Greenpoint, founded in 2017 by Jesse Reed and Hamish Smyth, with a second office in Miami.

Its approach is research-based, systematic and practical, and its clients include Knoll, Chapter and Groove.

It also runs its own type foundry, which matters if your identity needs a custom typeface.

Hyperakt

Hyperakt is a branding agency for nonprofits and foundations, and a certified New York City Women-Owned Business Enterprise.

Its clients include the Ford Foundation, The New York Community Trust, NYCLU and DonorsChoose.

Start here if your organization is mission-driven and the brand has to survive board review.

High Tide

High Tide works across brand identity, art direction, packaging and web design for Aimé Leon Dore, Warby Parker, Seed and Inness.

Its own site states no address, so confirm where the team actually sits if being local matters to you.

The work is strongest where an identity has to carry through packaging, space and digital at once.

PORTO ROCHA

PORTO ROCHA describes itself as a global strategy and design agency with offices in New York and London.

Its projects include Nike Run, MoMA PS1, Kunsthalle Basel and Robinhood.

Study this work when an identity has to move between cultural storytelling and a very large public audience.

Athletics

Athletics is a brand innovation studio on North 6th Street in Williamsburg, combining designers, strategists and technologists.

Its clients include Salesforce, the New Museum, Google Chrome and Soccer.com.

A good fit when a brand needs both a strong visual system and the tools to run it.

&Walsh

&Walsh is a New York creative agency working across brand strategy, art direction, design and production.

Its projects include &Lex, &Plenty, &Zooba and Google I/O 2023.

Expect bold, high-contrast work that is built to be noticed.

Pentagram

Pentagram calls itself the world’s largest independent design consultancy, with 23 partners and a New York office on Park Avenue South.

Its recent work includes the Obama Presidential Center, Isomorphic Labs and the Guggenheim.

Each partner runs their own team, so you are choosing a partner as much as a firm.

Chermayeff & Geismar & Haviv

Chermayeff & Geismar & Haviv is an independent New York firm specializing in trademarks and identity programs, on West 24th Street.

Its recent clients include the U.S. Open, NBC, America250 and the Warner Bros. family of brands.

I worked with this firm, and its belief that a mark should be appropriate, memorable and simple still shapes how I design.

Red Antler

Red Antler is a New York branding agency founded in 2007 and best known for launching consumer startups.

Its clients include Cotopaxi, Hinge, Elm Biosciences and McKinsey.

Consider it when a launch needs brand, advertising and media handled together rather than in sequence.

One studio named in the previous version of this guide has been dropped, because I could not reach its site to verify a single current claim about it.

For a fuller look at the agency end of this market, I keep a separate roundup of branding agencies in NYC.

Does your designer actually need to be in New York?

Honestly, for most identity projects, no — and I say that as someone who would benefit from telling you otherwise.

Logo and identity work is reviewed on a screen, approved on a screen, and delivered as files.

I run week-long sprints for clients in London, Sydney, Dublin and Mississippi without anyone getting on a plane.

Being local does matter in three specific situations.

If the brand lives in a physical place — a restaurant, a hotel, a dispensary, a gallery — a designer who can stand in the room will make better decisions about signage, menus and materials.

If your team is large and the identity has to survive internal politics, a designer who can run a workshop in your office will get to agreement faster than six video calls would.

And if you want to review physical proofs — printed stock, packaging substrates, embroidery, foil — proximity saves real weeks.

Outside those three cases, hire the best brief match you can find and treat the zip code as a tiebreaker.

The one genuine New York advantage is density of adjacent talent: photographers, printers, fabricators, sign shops and developers who already work together.

What brand identity design costs in New York

New York prices are higher than the national average for the same scope, and the gap is widest at the studio and agency end.

An independent NYC designer with real identity experience generally quotes in the low to mid thousands for a logo and core system.

A small New York studio typically starts in the tens of thousands once strategy, naming or packaging are included.

The firms at the top of this page — Pentagram, PORTO ROCHA, Red Antler — are working at a different order of magnitude again, because they are selling a rollout rather than a mark.

The number that matters is the price for an agreed scope, not an hourly rate.

Ask every designer to state what is included, how many directions you will see, how many revision rounds are covered, which final files you receive, and who owns the artwork afterwards.

I have broken the whole market down, tier by tier, in my logo design cost guide, and the branding package guide covers what belongs in a complete engagement.

My own rate is published rather than quoted case by case: a flat $3,000 per week, with the number of weeks agreed before work starts, on my pricing page.

How to vet a New York designer before you hire

New York has the deepest freelance design market in the country, which also makes it the easiest place to mis-hire.

Separate agency credits from personal work.

A large share of the designers here have worked at Pentagram, Red Antler, Order or Wolff Olins, and those credits are real but they are team credits.

Ask which part of the project was theirs, and whether they have led a comparable project alone since.

Check whether freelancing is the job or the side of the job.

Several excellent designers in this city freelance around a full-time role, which is fine if you know it and a problem if you do not.

You can usually tell from their own résumé page, and I have flagged it above where a site makes it explicit.

Confirm availability before you fall in love with a portfolio.

One designer on this list publishes the month she is next booking; another lists bookings opening in 2027.

Make sure the portfolio is current.

A site still labelled with a two-year-old date usually means the practice has moved on, in one direction or another.

Beyond the portfolios here, Contra and Upwork are useful for finding people who sell freelance services, while Behance and Dribbble are better for discovering visual work than for assessing a practice.

Treat any profile as a starting point and follow it through to the designer’s own site before you make contact.

What to prepare before you reach out

You do not need a finished strategy document, but a short written brief will change the quality of every conversation you have.

  • The business: what you sell, who it is for, and what makes it different.
  • The challenge: what is not working, or what you are about to launch.
  • The scope: identity only, or packaging, website, motion, or some combination.
  • The timing: the real deadline and anything it depends on.
  • The budget: a working range, so the designer can propose a scope that fits it.
  • The decision-makers: who gives feedback and who signs off.

The last one causes more delays than every other item combined.

If four people have to agree, say so on the first call, because it changes how the project should be run.

Work with me on your brand identity

If you want to work directly with an independent designer on strategy, identity and a website, here is what that looks like in practice.

You brief one person, that person designs the work, and nothing passes through an account layer on the way to you.

My recent projects include Airport Executive, Fox Berman, SweetGrass, Aero and Periti Digital.

They cover luxury transport, legal services, cannabis retail, health technology and B2B consulting, which is deliberate: the method travels further than any one aesthetic.

I can take the identity through to the places people actually meet your business, including web design, development and motion where the project calls for it.

Book a call to talk about what you are building and whether my approach fits it.

Hiring a brand identity designer in NYC: FAQ

How much does a logo designer cost in NYC?

An experienced independent designer in New York generally charges in the low to mid thousands for a logo and core identity system.

Small studios usually start in the tens of thousands once strategy or packaging is included, and the largest firms work in six figures.

My own rate is a flat $3,000 per week, with a complete brand identity delivered in one week.

Should I hire a freelance designer or a New York agency?

Hire a freelancer when you want the senior person to do the work and you need to move quickly.

Hire an agency when the rollout spans many markets, channels or internal teams and you need project management as much as design.

For most founders and small teams, an independent designer delivers better thinking per dollar than a mid-sized agency will.

Does my brand identity designer need to be based in New York?

Usually not, because identity work is reviewed and delivered digitally.

Being local genuinely helps in three cases: when the brand lives in a physical space, when a large team needs an in-person workshop to reach agreement, and when you want to approve printed or packaging proofs in person.

Otherwise, hire the closest match to your brief.

How do I check that a New York designer is really independent?

Read their own résumé or about page for a current employer.

Many talented New York designers freelance alongside a full-time role, which affects their availability and their response times.

Ask directly how many projects they are running, when they can start, and whether anyone else will touch the work.

How long does a brand identity project take in New York?

From one week to about three months, depending on scope and on how quickly you give feedback.

A focused identity sprint can finish in a week, a studio engagement typically runs six to twelve weeks, and a full agency rebrand runs longer.

Slow internal approvals are the most common reason projects overrun.

What should I receive when the project ends?

Vector master artwork plus exports for screen and print.

That means SVG or EPS source files, PNG and PDF exports, every approved lockup including a single-colour version, colour values in HEX, RGB, CMYK and Pantone, named typefaces with their licensing, brand guidelines, and written transfer of ownership to you.

Where do New York brand designers actually find clients?

Mostly through referrals, past clients and their own sites rather than through marketplaces.

Contra and Upwork are useful for finding people who openly sell freelance services, while Behance and Dribbble are better for discovering visual work.

Whichever you use, follow through to the designer’s own site and check credits, availability and how recent the work is.

What is the difference between a logo and a brand identity?

A logo is one mark; a brand identity is the whole system that mark sits inside.

An identity includes the logo plus colour, typography, layout rules, imagery, motion and the guidelines that let your team apply all of it without you.

Buying only a logo is the most common reason a new brand looks inconsistent three months after launch.

Final thoughts

The best brand identity designer for your business is the one whose work, experience, timeline and way of working match what you actually need.

I would start with three portfolios that feel relevant, read complete projects rather than single marks, and talk to each designer about the brief before comparing any proposals.

A recognizable client name is useful context, but the better question is who did the work and how they would approach your particular problem.

Whether you choose an independent designer or a studio, look for clear thinking, a clear process and a scope you both understand.

And if you want to work directly with me on your identity, explore my case studies and book a call.
intro:
If you are hiring a brand identity designer in NYC, the hard part is not finding one.

It is working out which of the many people calling themselves brand designers here is actually independent, actually available, and actually right for your brief.

I am Arek Dvornechuck, a senior freelance brand identity and web designer based in Brooklyn, and I have included my own practice below so you can compare it with the rest.

I built this list by reading portfolios the way I would read a competitor’s, and I checked every site on it again in October 2026.
